articles.title: I finally visited this rugged Canadian island. Coastal hikes and live music were just the start.
articles.summary: Beyond its dramatic views, Cape Breton Island delivers fresh seafood, live music, breathtaking hikes and so much more.
articles.body:
Even though it's relatively close to where I live on the East Coast, Cape Breton Island in Nova Scotia has existed in my mind as some far-off land that, maybe one day, I would be lucky to explore. That day came this summer when I finally made the trip with my husband and our baby daughter.

Our goal: to explore and take in as much lobster, fiddle music and hiking as we could.

Cape Breton Island has a fascinating blend of culture and history. It has been home to the Mi'kmaq people for over 10,000 years. It was settled by Acadians in the 1700s and had a large influx of Scottish immigrants in the 1800s. Those influences continue to be felt today across the food, language, craft and music traditions.

In the course of a week, we would explore the island, making sure to drive along the famed Cabot Trail, hike in Cape Breton Highlands National Park, stay in a rural Acadian village, hear local music performances and feast on the freshest seafood.

Given the island's distance from the nearest international airport (over four hours), we opted to spend the first and last nights of our trip in Halifax, Nova Scotia's capital and a charming coastal city that warrants a trip of its own.

Here are the things you won't want to miss if you travel to Cape Breton.

You'll be hard-pressed to arrive on the island without people asking if you plan to explore the Cabot Trail. This 185-mile loop on the northern end of the island runs through Cape Breton Highlands National Park and connects coastline, villages, hiking trails and vistas in one drivable loop. The trail can be tackled in its entirety or enjoyed in segments.

Since we were traveling with a baby (who isn't the biggest fan of the car), we chose to stay near the park in the Acadian community of Chéticamp, rather than circumnavigate the island. Chéticamp was a perfect home base for exploring some of the Cabot Trail's most scenic hikes and great lobster spots, and it meant we didn't need to spend endless hours in the car.

In Chéticamp, we were very near the Skyline Trail , a relatively flat four-mile out-and-back hike that's arguably the park's most popular and scenic. We also weren't far from The Lone Shieling Trail , a short hike that winds through a grove of 350-year-old sugar maple trees. On the latter, we found ourselves alone in one of the largest groves of old-growth hardwood trees in the Maritimes, surrounded by thousands of wildflowers. It's my favorite memory of the trip.

Before setting out, make sure to check in with the visitor center. If you're planning to hike the Skyline Trail between June 26 and October 25, 2026, you must book a timed parking reservation online in advance.

Experience the culture and cuisine of an Acadian village

Several new businesses — many with deep roots in the community — have sprung up in this corner of Cape Breton. Among them is LaPointe Chalets , a collection of six private, eco-friendly cabins on Chéticamp Island overlooking the coast. We stayed here and loved how quiet and private the property was. With our own chalet, we had room to spread out, could cook outside on our barbecue and watch late-evening sunsets from Adirondack chairs on our private deck overlooking the water.

Another recent addition is Doucet , an inventive restaurant serving a multicourse tasting menu inspired by the area's Acadian heritage. And the newly opened Bistro Fiset serves local lobster, Nova Scotia oysters and craft cocktails.

In town, we loved Marguerite , a modern general store that was stocked with everything from fresh blueberry scones and locally made kelp lip balm to vintage wool coats from Montreal. We also visited Les Trois Pignons , a seasonal museum and cultural center dedicated to Chéticamp's centuries-old Acadian rug hooking tradition. For more locally made crafts, we went to Freya & Thor , which sells art and handcrafted goods from local artisans (think: lip balm made with Nova Scotian kelp, prints by Cape Breton watercolorists) plus seriously good coffee and pastries.

Cape Breton Island is known for its unique fiddle tradition, which evolved from the fiddle music brought over by Scottish Gaels beginning in the late 18th century. It's often lively, upbeat and feels like a natural backdrop for zipping around the island.

While you may stumble upon some music in restaurants and pubs (or even on the radio in your rental car), you may want to plan some distinct stops. Consider attending a ceilidh, a traditional Gaelic gathering with music, dancing and more. There's even a Ceilidh Trail : a 67-mile stretch of highway along the western coast that passes through areas known for Gaelic culture and music.

Or, drop by the Celtic Music Interpretive Centre to learn more about the music traditions of the island, attend a concert or join in for a ceilidh. One of the island's most famous music venues is the Red Shoe Pub in Mabou, which regularly hosts live music. Glenora (considered the oldest single-malt whisky distillery in North America) also hosts regular music sessions.

You can detect the Scottish heritage in Cape Breton in a variety of ways, including the fiddle music and plentiful golf courses. The island is something of a destination for golf lovers, and many head to Cabot in the beach town of Inverness. There, you can book a tee time or just soak in the incredible views from the Cabot Cliffs course.

Even if you're not a golfer, Cabot Cape Breton is one of the island's most luxurious places to stay, and it offers a range of accommodations from rooms to full vacation rentals. We loved spending time on the Cabot Cliffs overlooking the Northumberland Strait.

Our dinner at Cabot's Coore's Lobster Shack was also a highlight. Located in a barn-like building, the lobster was served family-style, swimming in a pan of hot butter, and to the uptempo swings of live fiddle music. It was the perfect ending to our time on Cape Breton Island.

articles.title: O que fizeram os candidatos ao governo de PE nesta sexta | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira atividades de Guilherme Fonseca (PSTU), Ivan Moraes (PSOL), João Campos (PSB), Professora Camila (UP), Raquel Lyra (PSD), Renan Hallais (Missão) e Victor Assis (PCO).
articles.summary: Confira atividades de Guilherme Fonseca (PSTU), Ivan Moraes (PSOL), João Campos (PSB), Professora Camila (UP), Raquel Lyra (PSD), Renan Hallais (Missão) e Victor Assis (PCO).
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco nas eleições 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

Candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco cumpriram agendas de campanha nesta sexta-feira (2), dois dias antes das eleições, que acontecem no domingo (4) . Entre os compromissos, houve panfletagens, caminhadas e "porta a porta" no Grande Recife e no interior.

Durante agenda em Jaboatão dos Guararapes , João Campos ( PSB ) prometeu triplicar parte da BR-101 e realizar obras de infraestrutura para a Região Metropolitana. Já a candidata Raquel Lyra ( PSD ) prometeu implantar corredores cicloviários no Grande Recife durante agenda no bairro da Imbiribeira, na Zona Sul da capital.

Os candidatos Renan Santos ( Missão ) e Victor Assis ( PCO ) não enviaram as agendas de campanha até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Veja como foram as agendas dos candidatos (por ordem alfabética):

Segundo a agenda do candidato, Guilherme Fonseca fez panfletagem pela manhã na Estação Recife do metrô, no bairro de São José, no Centro da capital. No fim da tarde, participou de outra panfletagem no Conjunto Residencial Ignêz Andreazza, no bairro de Areias, na Zona Oeste do Recife.

Segundo a agenda do candidato, Ivan Moraes iniciou o dia com uma visita à Associação de Surdos de Pernambuco, no bairro da Boa Vista, no Centro do Recife. Em seguida, realizou panfletagens no bairro das Graças, na Zona Norte, no Mercado de São José e novamente na Boa Vista, na área central da capital.

No fim da tarde, participou de um encontro na sede da Central Única dos Trabalhadores (CUT), no bairro de Santo Amaro, onde aderiu à Plataforma de Compromisso com a Classe Trabalhadora da entidade.

João Campos cumpriu agenda em cidades do Grande Recife. Durante compromisso em Jaboatão dos Guararapes, ele prometeu triplicar um trecho da BR-101 e realizar obras de infraestrutura para a Região Metropolitana.

O candidato também fez uma caminhada de porta em porta no Recife, uma caravana em Ipojuca e minicarreatas em São Lourenço da Mata , Camaragibe e Recife.

Professora Camila (UP) participou de um comício no Centro do Recife ao lado da candidata à Presidência da República pelo partido, Samara Martins . Depois, fez uma caminhada até a Estação Recife, no bairro de São José.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição Raquel Lyra iniciou a agenda de campanha com um panfletaço no bairro da Imbiribeira, na Zona Sul da capital. Durante o compromisso, prometeu implantar corredores cicloviários no Grande Recife caso seja reeleita.

À noite, participou de carreatas em Gravatá , no Agreste, e em Vitória de Santo Antão , na Zona da Mata.

articles.title: 75-year-old Kerala man dies of heart attack during CJP protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A 75-year-old man from Kerala died after suffering a heart attack while attending the CJP protest at Shivaji Park in Mumbai on Friday evening.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A 75-year-old man from Kerala died after suffering a heart attack while attending the CJP protest at Shivaji Park in Mumbai on Friday evening.The deceased was identified as Gopalakrishna Subbaiya Pillai, a resident of Dosti West County, B Wing, Thane. He had arrived at Shivaji Park around 4.30pm to witness the protest.Police said Pillai, a Keralite, had come to Mumbai and was staying in Thane. On Friday, he travelled from Thane to Dadar to attend the protest. Around 5pm, he complained of chest pain.With the assistance of his friend and police personnel deployed at the protest site, Pillai was taken to Sushrusha Hospital at Shivaji Park for treatment.Policemen at the spot tried to revive him with CPR, but their efforts failed. articles.title: What's a golden spurtle and why do so  many people want one?
articles.summary: The World Porridge Championships are back with the biggest field yet and a fight for the Golden Spurtle.
articles.body:
What does a bakery owner from San Francisco have in common with a retired British Army officer, a newly-qualified Scottish lawyer, a US Marine veteran, an Edinburgh artist and a teacher from Fife?

All of them - plus a 2026 MasterChef UK finalist - are preparing to fight for the title of World Porridge Making Champion.

The annual oat-off has never been more popular, with double the number of entrants than the previous highest turnout.

The hopefuls all want to leave the Highland village of Carrbridge carrying the Golden Spurtle, porridge making's most coveted award.

The trophy is a giant version of the traditional wooden tool used for stirring porridge, thick soups, and stew.

The surge in porridge popularity could be fuelled by the success of the highly acclaimed documentary film The Golden Spurtle, which followed competitors at the 2023 championships.

Its focus on the competition's eccentric characters, intense porridge-making rivalries, and porridge world legends like Carrbridge local Ian Bishop and the "queen of porridge" Lisa Williams, has inspired record numbers to try their hand at competitive breakfast-making.

Thirty competitors representing 14 countries will take part - from Australia, the Czech Republic, South Africa, the USA, Norway, France, Switzerland and the Netherlands, as well as from across the UK and Ireland.

Among them will be defending world porridge making champion Sven Seljom from Norway, together with national porridge champions from competitions in the Netherlands, Norway and Australia.

Sven is taking part in the main competition, where competitors must prepare traditional porridge using only three ingredients - oatmeal, water and salt.

He can't wait: "The village and the organisers are doing such a tremendous job and it was the greatest experience of my life winning the title last year," he said.

There is also a speciality porridge competition, where competitors can combine oatmeal with any ingredients they choose, resulting in an imaginative mix of sweet and savoury dishes.

Last year's Speciality Award winner, Caroline Velik from Australia, created porridge jaffles – yoghurt flatbreads filled with porridge, rum-soaked bananas and toffee rum liqueur, and tossed in plum sugar.

The boss of it all - Porridge Chieftain Alan Rankin - said the response to this year's competition was unprecedented.

"The documentary has introduced the competition, Carrbridge, and the wonderful world of porridge to a whole new audience, and we're really looking forward to welcoming this year's competitors to the village," he said.

Robert Reid, who won Australia's first national competition, the Pearly Spurtle, will be competing in Scotland as part of his prize.

He said: "It's been a bit of a whirlwind. To go from my wife telling me she submitted my application to actually winning the Pearly Spurtle four weeks later has been pretty surreal.

"My dad is Scottish, so porridge has been part of my life for as long as I can remember. The sense of community at the Pearly Spurtle was incredible, I'm excited to now have the chance to do them proud in Carrbridge."

He said salted porridge had shaped his life, thanks to his Scottish granny and his Dad, who was born on the Isle of Jura and raised in Greenock.

"Their tradition lives on in my own kitchen, where my twins now enjoy properly salted, never sweet porridge cooked by me or their grandad," he said.

"Winning the Pearly Spurtle was a proud moment, especially using my dad's treasured Scottish spurtle. The same one I will bring with me to Carrbridge and the Golden Spurtle to represent Australia."

articles.standfirst: Resumo de notícias entre os dias 26 de setembro e 2 de outubro no g1 Zona da Mata.
articles.summary: Resumo de notícias entre os dias 26 de setembro e 2 de outubro no g1 Zona da Mata.
articles.body:
Olá! Entre as notícias que mais chamaram a atenção dos leitores do g1 Zona da Mata nesta semana estão histórias de solidariedade, cuidado com o meio ambiente e sorte.

Relembre três dos destaques publicados entre os dias 26 de setembro e 2 de outubro :

Único espectador de apresentação da filha

O pai que viralizou nas redes sociais depois de aparecer como o único espectador da apresentação da filha em uma faculdade de Muriaé enfrentou chuva e foi de moto até o local para ajudá-la.

Gilberto Ferreira Berriel, de 69 anos, estava com uma costela quebrada e 20 pontos em cada um dos dois dedos feridos de uma das mãos após sofrer um acidente de moto. Mesmo machucado, decidiu sair de casa quando a filha, Monalisa Barriel, de 18 anos, contou que precisava de um carregador para fazer a apresentação.

Ele levou o equipamento e permaneceu no local para acompanhar a filha. Monalisa apresentava, com colegas do curso de Análise e Desenvolvimento de Sistemas, um site de uma cartilha de prevenção contra a violência doméstica.

“Eu saí de cima da cama para ir lá levar o carregador e fazer presença com ela. Porque eu gosto muito da minha filha e faço tudo o que posso por ela”, contou Gilberto ao g1.

Aos 78 anos, José Correia da Rosa encontrou uma maneira de ocupar os dias da aposentadoria: plantar árvores frutíferas. Há quase 7 anos, ele cultiva um verdadeiro pomar na Via São Pedro , em Juiz de Fora . Até agora, já são cerca de 150 árvores plantadas no local.

A história ganhou repercussão depois que a bióloga Júlia Firjam registrou o trabalho de José e divulgou imagens nas redes sociais. Ele conta que pretende continuar plantando enquanto tiver saúde e disposição.

“Enquanto Deus me der saúde, como Ele me dá, eu vou plantando… Ele quem me repõe a força de vontade de ir pra lá”, disse.

Aposta de JF ganha mais de meio milhão na Lotofácil

O vencedor ou vencedora vai receber R$ 510.692,35. A aposta foi registrada em uma agência que fica na Rua Diva Garcia.

Uma aposta simples feita em uma lotérica do bairro Linhares, em Juiz de Fora, acertou os 15 números do concurso 3792 da Lotofácil, sorteado na terça-feira (29).

As dezenas sorteadas foram 02, 04, 06, 07, 08, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 20, 23, 24 e 25.

Outra aposta feita na mesma lotérica também foi premiada: acertou 14 números e levou R$ 33.254,55.

articles.title: Voo para Israel: copiloto atacou piloto com machado | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o procurador-geral dos Emirados Árabes Unidos, copiloto tentou assumir o controle do avião durante voo de Dubai para Tel Aviv; investigação ainda está em andamento.
articles.summary: Segundo o procurador-geral dos Emirados Árabes Unidos, copiloto tentou assumir o controle do avião durante voo de Dubai para Tel Aviv; investigação ainda está em andamento.
articles.body:
Os Emirados Árabes Unidos disseram neste sábado (3) que o copiloto do voo da FlyDubai atacou o comandante com um machado de emergência e tentou assumir o controle da aeronave durante o incidente ocorrido na quarta-feira (30).

Até então, não estava claro qual arma havia sido usada no ataque. Segundo o procurador-geral dos Emirados, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, o episódio foi uma tentativa de ato "terrorista"

O voo FZ1073, que seguia de Dubai para Tel Aviv, transportava mais de 170 passageiros e tripulantes quando o incidente aconteceu na quarta-feira.

Passageiros e tripulantes conseguiram dominar o copiloto. Um piloto reserva da FlyDubai que estava a bordo assumiu o controle da aeronave e pousou no aeroporto de Tabuk, no noroeste da Arábia Saudita, onde o copiloto foi detido.

Segundo a Reuters, o copiloto foi identificado como Hammam al-Hammami, cidadão de Omã, por uma fonte com conhecimento direto do caso. As autoridades dos Emirados Árabes Unidos não confirmaram imediatamente a identidade.

A investigação ainda está em andamento para determinar as circunstâncias do episódio, a motivação do copiloto e se houve outras pessoas envolvidas. As autoridades também analisam evidências físicas e digitais.

A classificação do episódio como tentativa de ataque "terrorista" é a primeira feita publicamente por uma autoridade dos Emirados. Até então, as circunstâncias e a motivação do ataque ainda eram investigadas.

A FlyDubai afirmou que as circunstâncias do incidente continuam sob investigação e que a companhia não está em posição de comentar mais detalhes.

O avião saiu de Dubai com destino a Tel Aviv. Durante o voo sobre a Arábia Saudita, a aeronave perdeu cerca de 5 mil metros de altitude em pouco mais de 30 segundos, segundo dados do Flightradar24.

O comandante foi atacado dentro da cabine. A nova versão apresentada pelas autoridades dos Emirados afirma que o copiloto usou um machado de emergência, equipamento mantido na cabine para situações de emergência.

Depois do ataque, o comandante conseguiu abrir a porta da cabine. Passageiros e tripulantes ajudaram a conter o copiloto, enquanto outro piloto que estava a bordo assumiu os controles.

A aeronave pousou em segurança em Tabuk, na Arábia Saudita.

Autoridades dos Emirados e de Israel participam da investigação. Os investigadores buscam esclarecer o que aconteceu dentro da cabine, a motivação do copiloto e se ele agiu sozinho ou recebeu orientação de outras pessoas.

O primeiro-ministro de Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu, havia dito anteriormente que o copiloto era cidadão de Omã e que poderia ter passado por radicalização islamista. Ele também afirmou que ainda não havia sido estabelecida uma motivação definitiva para o ataque. A investigação continua.

O avião que transportava passageiros que estavam no voo da FlyDubai com destino a Israel, saído dos Emirados Árabes Unidos e desviado para a Arábia Saudita após emitir um sinal de emergência, chega ao Aeroporto Internacional Ben Gurion, em Lod, perto de Tel Aviv, Israel. — Foto: Ammar Awad / Reuters

articles.title: Motosserra e moedor de carne: provas de assassinato de modelo chocam | G1
articles.standfirst: Abby Choi, de 28 anos, foi encontrada morta em fevereiro de 2023. Ex-marido e familiares são acusados de assassinar a jovem.
articles.summary: Abby Choi, de 28 anos, foi encontrada morta em fevereiro de 2023. Ex-marido e familiares são acusados de assassinar a jovem.
articles.body:
Abby Choi, modelo e influenciadora de Hong Kong que foi encontrada morta aos 28 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Uma motosserra, um martelo e um moedor de carne foram apresentados nesta sexta-feira (2) durante o julgamento pelo assassinato da modelo e influenciadora Abby Choi , de 28 anos. O caso, que envolve uma disputa familiar, chocou Hong Kong , onde crimes desse tipo são raros.

O corpo esquartejado da modelo foi encontrado pela polícia em fevereiro de 2023, em uma propriedade nos arredores da cidade. Poucos dias antes de morrer, Choi, que tinha 140 mil seguidores no Instagram, havia publicado fotos da Semana de Moda de Paris.

O assassinato é atribuído ao ex-marido da modelo, Alex Kwong, de 31 anos, ao pai dele, Kwong Kau, de 68, e ao irmão, Anthony Kwong, de 35.

Segundo a acusação, o crime foi motivado por uma disputa financeira envolvendo um imóvel de luxo, pelo qual Choi pagou mais de US$ 7,5 milhões (cerca de R$ 39 milhões).

Os três acusados, que podem ser condenados à prisão perpétua, declararam-se inocentes na quarta-feira (30), primeiro dia do julgamento, que deve se estender até dezembro.

Nesta sexta-feira (2), a promotora Charlotte Draycott afirmou que o assassinato foi resultado de um plano "cuidadosamente elaborado".

Segundo ela, os acusados compraram, dias antes do crime, ferramentas que seriam usadas para esquartejar e se desfazer do corpo, incluindo um moedor de carne.

A promotora Charlotte Draycott afirmou que Kwong e seus familiares compraram, dias antes, as ferramentas que seriam usadas para esquartejar e se desfazer do corpo, incluindo um moedor de carne.

Uma vizinha relatou ter ouvido o barulho de uma motosserra no prédio onde, posteriormente, foi encontrada uma lâmina de serra com vestígios de carne humana, afirmou a promotora.

A acusação também apresentou ao júri um martelo que, segundo um laudo forense, tinha formato compatível com as lesões encontradas no crânio da vítima.

Imagens de câmeras de segurança exibidas no tribunal mostram Choi entrando em uma das duas vans usadas pela família Kwong em 21 de fevereiro de 2023. Os veículos foram estacionados perto da propriedade onde a polícia encontrou os restos mortais da modelo, três dias depois.

O ex-sogro e o ex-cunhado de Choi foram presos em 24 de fevereiro. O ex-marido, com quem ela tinha dois filhos, foi detido no dia seguinte, quando, segundo a polícia, planejava fugir de Hong Kong .

articles.summary: Primeiro turno acontece neste domingo (4), com projeção de disputa acirrada entre ACM Neto (União Brasil) e Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT).
articles.body:
Candidatos ao governo da Bahia foram entrevistados pelo BMD de 14 a 19 de setembro — Foto: Reprodução/TV Bahia | Arte g1

Promessas de campanha, cobranças, polarização entre os dois maiores candidatos na disputa e o reforço de alianças nacionais foram os destaques da campanha pelo governo da Bahia neste ano. O primeiro turno das eleições acontece neste domingo (4), com ACM Neto ( União Brasil ) e Jerônimo Rodrigues ( PT ) à frente da disputa.

Além do ex-prefeito de Salvador e do atual governador, que busca a reeleição, Ronaldo Mansur ( PSOL ), Aroldo Félix ( Unidade Popular ), Ariel Capistrano (DC) e Maria Bona ( PCO ) concorrem ao posto de chefe do Executivo estadual. Os eleitores deverão ainda votar para presidente, senador (dois nomes), deputado federal e deputado estadual.

Desde agosto, quando o período oficial de campanha começou, os candidatos buscam reforçar suas diferenças por meio das associações com os candidatos à Presidência.

De um lado, Jerônimo reforça que é o candidato do "time de Lula", em referência à aliança partidária com o atual presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). A campanha do governador também busca associar Neto, seu principal adversário, à família Bolsonaro.

Já o ex-prefeito de Salvador repete, em sua campanha, que teve gestões bem sucedidas em paralelo à atuação de diferentes presidentes. Publicamente, ele declarou apoio a Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), ex-governador de Goiás que agora concorre à Presidência.

Assuntos como acesso à educação, infraestrutura e transporte público foram abordados nos discursos dos candidatos ao governo do estado. Entretanto, conforme a última pesquisa realizada pela Quaest , divulgada no dia 24 de setembro, os eleitores apontam que questões ligadas à violência (40%) e saúde (34%) são os principais problemas do estado.

Esse cenário se refletiu nas falas públicas dos candidatos, que enfatizaram propostas para essas áreas. Os dois temas dominaram as discussões durante a corrida eleitoral e pautaram a maioria das peças de campanha dos postulantes ao cargo de governador.

No âmbito da segurança pública, o avanço das facções criminosas na Região Metropolitana de Salvador (RMS) e a presença de cinco municípios da Bahia na lista das dez cidades mais violentas do Brasil estão entre as problemáticas mais abordadas.

O candidato ACM Neto, que, segundo as pesquisas de intenção de voto, está tecnicamente empatado com Jerônimo Rodrigues, usou esses pontos para atacar o rival em entrevistas. Ele apresentou propostas, como a implementação de uma "Governadoria da Segurança" , por meio da qual monitoraria, pessoalmente, as ações das forças de segurança no estado.

Por sua vez, Jerônimo Rodrigues não participou de debates e enfatizou sua relação com o atual presidente, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, durante atos de campanha. Partindo de propostas de continuidade, o candidato enfatizou planos de fortalecimento do efetivo policial com a contratação de novos profissionais e concursos como uma alternativa para solução de problemas ligados à segurança pública.

Urna eletrônica — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

No quesito saúde, os destaques foram a fila da regulação para procedimentos médicos em unidades do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) e o fornecimento de atendimento especializado em cidades do interior da Bahia. As problemáticas também foram espaço de disputa narrativa entre Jerônimo Rodrigues e ACM Neto, que apresentaram diferentes perspectivas para lidar com a situação. Ambos se apoiaram em uma abordagem regional para abordar o tema, destacando as dificuldades que moradores de cidades do interior têm em acessar procedimentos especializados de saúde.

O candidato do União Brasil defendeu o chamado "PIX Saúde", que defende a compra de leitos para o desafogamento da demanda em unidades do SUS , como uma solução. Já Jerônimo prometeu a expansão da infraestrutura hospitalar no estado, com a ampliação descentralizada das unidades de saúde na Bahia.

Distantes da dicotomia política protagonizada por ACM Neto e Jerônimo Rodrigues, Ronaldo Mansur (PSOL), Aroldo Félix (Unidade Popular), Ariel Capistrano (DC) e Maria Bona (PCO) utilizaram brechas para discutir temas ligados à educação e políticas econômicas .

Mansur sugeriu o fim gradual do regime de contratos temporários (Reda), defendeu a realização contínua de concursos para professores e a promoção de uma reforma agrária para lidar com os conflitos por terra que acontecem nas regiões sul e extremo sul do estado. A valorização da carreira de educador também esteve presente nas falas públicas de Aroldo Félix, que chegou a defender, em entrevista na Central de Eleições da TV Bahia, a contratação de mais professores.

O investimento na qualificação profissional e a criação de oportunidades de acesso ao primeiro emprego foi trabalhado pelo candidato Ariel Capistrano durante entrevista à TV Bahia. Já Maria Bona defendeu a gestão coletiva de instituições de ensino no estado, enfatizando uma gestão transparente de recursos públicos.

A força do eleitorado das cidades do interior do estado pautou as agendas políticas dos candidatos ao governo do estado durante a trajetória eleitoral até o primeiro turno das eleições. A fim de reunir apoiadores, muitos realizaram atos de campanha e comícios em municípios do interior.

No caso da campanha de ACM Neto, por exemplo, as regiões oeste e sudoeste do estado foram muito visitadas. O candidato deu ênfase aos problemas estruturais na saúde pública e infraestrutura nas regiões desde o início de sua agenda eleitoral, começando a campanha eleitoral na cidade de Carinhanha.

Jerônimo Rodrigues realizou seu primeiro ato de campanha em Salvador, mas também participou de caminhadas e comícios em cidades do interior do estado. Em seus discursos, o candidato também deu destaque a ações que pretende realizar nos municípios do oeste da Bahia.

Já os candidatos Ronaldo Mansur (PSOL), Aroldo Félix (Unidade Popular) e Ariel Capistrano (DC) concentraram os atos de campanha em Salvador, fazendo poucas movimentações para cidades longe da região metropolitana.

Na maior parte do tempo, a candidata Maria Bona (PCO) realizou atos de campanha na cidade de Rio de Contas , na Chapada Diamantina, onde vive. Em entrevista à TV Bahia, ela chegou a ser questionada sobre planos para expandir as ações de campanha e destacou que o partido enfrenta dificuldades financeiras.

articles.title: Ao lado de Lula, Haddad faz último ato de campanha na Av. Paulista neste sábado; Tarcísio prioriza interior com Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Campanha do atual governador informou que prefeitos aliados organizarão atos em diferentes regiões do estado. Candidatas ao Senado, Marina Silva (Rede) e Simone Tebet (PSB) confirmaram participação no ato do PT.
articles.summary: Campanha do atual governador informou que prefeitos aliados organizarão atos em diferentes regiões do estado. Candidatas ao Senado, Marina Silva (Rede) e Simone Tebet (PSB) confirmaram participação no ato do PT.
articles.body:
Tarcísio e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), e Fernando Haddad e Lula (PT). — Foto: Montagem/g1/Divulgação

Os candidatos ao governo de São Paulo encerram suas campanhas de rua neste sábado (3), às vésperas do 1º turno das eleições. Tarcísio de Freitas ( Republicanos ), que disputa a reeleição, participará de uma carreata com Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) entre Santa Bárbara d'Oeste e Americana, no interior do estado. Já Fernando Haddad ( PT ) fará uma passeata a partir das 10h na região da Avenida Paulista, na capital, ao lado do presidente Lula (PT).

As duas agendas ocorrem no maior colégio eleitoral do país, que tem 34,1 milhões de eleitores.

A campanha de Tarcísio também informou que prefeitos aliados organizarão atos em diferentes regiões do estado. "Eu quero agradecer o apoio que eu recebi de todos os prefeitos nessa jornada", declarou o candidato.

As candidatas Marina Silva (Rede) e Simone Tebet (PSB), que tentam uma vaga no Senado, confirmaram participação no ato do PT.

A realização do ato de Haddad na Avenida Paulista chegou a ser alvo de um impasse entre a campanha petista e a Prefeitura de São Paulo.

Na quinta-feira (1º), a prefeitura afirmou que não havia autorizado a caminhada e disse que estava atendendo a uma requisição do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de São Paulo (TRE-SP). Segundo a administração municipal, o tribunal teria determinado que a Paulista fosse mantida desimpedida nos dias 3, 4, 24 e 25 de outubro.

No mesmo dia, porém, o TRE-SP afirmou que não havia determinado a proibição de atos políticos na Paulista no sábado. O tribunal esclareceu ao g1 que a solicitação feita à prefeitura era para que a avenida permanecesse aberta à circulação de veículos no domingo (4), dia da votação.

Nesta sexta (2), o TRE-SP decidiu, por maioria de votos, de 5 a 1, permitir a realização da "Caminhada Lula e Haddad" no sábado.

A decisão liminar foi tomada em mandado de segurança apresentado pela coligação Desperta São Paulo e suspendeu os efeitos de um ofício da Subprefeitura da Sé. O documento não recomendava a utilização da Rua Augusta e afirmava a impossibilidade de utilização da Avenida Paulista, o que, segundo o tribunal, tornava impraticável o trajeto previamente comunicado e ajustado pela campanha do PT sem indicar uma alternativa.

O governador fará sua última agenda de campanha nas ruas em uma carreata entre Santa Bárbara d'Oeste e Americana. Tarcísio estará ao lado de Flávio Bolsonaro, que também escolheu o interior paulista para seu último ato antes da votação.

O interior paulista tem histórico de maior apoio a candidatos de direita e centro-direita. Desde a redemocratização, em 1989, São Paulo elegeu principalmente governadores desse campo político.

As campanhas de Lula e Flávio não escolheram São Paulo por acaso . O estado concentra mais de 34 milhões de eleitores, e demonstrar interesse é uma oportunidade de buscar votos em uma região que concentra uma parcela importante do eleitorado do Sudeste.

Em 2022, o petista também encerrou sua campanha na Avenida Paulista. Naquele ano, Lula terminou a votação no estado com 44,8% dos votos válidos, contra 55,2% de Jair Bolsonaro (PL), uma diferença de 2,7 milhões de votos.

Lula busca manter a vantagem entre mulheres e católicos e avançar no Sudeste e no Nordeste. Já Flávio procura ampliar seu desempenho entre evangélicos e mulheres. Integrantes da campanha também afirmam que há espaço para aumentar a vantagem sobre Lula no Sudeste e reduzir a diferença no Nordeste.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo Eleições 2026: Chuva e calor no Vale do Paraíba | G1
articles.standfirst: Passagem de ventos atmosféricos deve provocar chuva no sábado (3); domingo, dia do primeiro turno, terá mais períodos de sol e possibilidade de pancadas à tarde.
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo para as Eleições 2026 no Vale do Paraíba indica chuva no sábado e domingo com sol, calor e risco de pancadas isoladas durante a tarde.
articles.body:
O fim de semana do primeiro turno das eleições de 2026 será marcado por mudanças no tempo no Vale do Paraíba e região. A passagem de ventos na atmosfera deve favorecer a ocorrência de chuva no sábado (3). Por outro lado, as temperaturas devem subir no domingo (4), dia da votação.

Segundo o meteorologista Gustavo Escobar, do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe), o sistema avança lentamente e deve influenciar as condições do tempo, principalmente no sábado.

“Esse cavado está avançando muito lentamente. A tendência é que ele atue durante o sábado e já se afaste. Ele que está provocando essas chuvas e trazendo essa umidade”, explica.

Tempo nublado, céu, previsão do tempo em Taubaté — Foto: Lucas Tavares/g1

No domingo, a previsão é de maiores períodos de sol, com elevação das temperaturas ao longo do dia. O calor, no entanto, pode favorecer a formação de pancadas de chuva à tarde.

“Domingo vai ser um dia com maiores aberturas de sol. O sol aparece, a temperatura sobe e, de tarde, o aquecimento diurno deve provocar algumas pancadas localizadas”, afirma Escobar.

A segunda-feira (5) deve seguir um cenário parecido: o dia começa com períodos de sol, mas há possibilidade de pancadas de chuva ao longo da tarde.

Por causa da possibilidade de chuva forte, a Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta para o estado de São Paulo. Em alguns pontos, a chuva pode ser intensa e vir acompanhada de raios e rajadas de vento.

articles.title: Candidatos ao governo do ES fazem campanha com foco na segurança | G1
articles.standfirst: Todos os cinco concorrentes disputam o cargo de governador pela primeira vez; programas de governo dos candidatos priorizam o combate ao crime organizado, a ampliação do ensino integral, melhorias na saúde e presença maior no interior.
articles.summary: Todos os concorrentes disputam o cargo de governador pela 1ª vez; programas de governo priorizam o combate ao crime organizado, a ampliação do ensino e melhoria da saúde.
articles.body:
Os candidatos ao governo do Espírito Santo em 2026: Breno Barcelos (Missão), Helder Salomão (PT), Lorenzo Pazolini (Republicanos), Rafael Demuner (UP) e Ricardo Ferraço (MDB) — Foto: Reprodução

O primeiro turno da disputa pelo governo do Espírito Santo em 2026 foi pautado por debates e propostas em torno da segurança pública, da saúde e da educação, além de trazer um elemento inédito: todos os cinco candidatos registrados disputam o cargo pela primeira vez.

Embora parte dos postulantes possua bagagem na vida pública — como mandatos como deputado federal, prefeito, vereador e até vice-governador e governador em exercício —, nenhum deles havia concorrido anteriormente ao posto mais alto do Executivo estadual.

A corrida eleitoral colocou em evidência diferentes visões sobre a gestão do estado e os problemas enfrentados pela população capixaba.

Entre os temas mais explorados nos programas de governo, sabatinas e debates de TV, destacaram-se o combate ao crime organizado e à violência contra a mulher , a ampliação do ensino em tempo integral , a valorização dos professores e discussões sobre a jornada de trabalho .

Nas ruas, a presença dos candidatos se dividiu entre agendas na Região Metropolitana de Vitória e articulações pelo interior do estado.

Veja os destaques da campanha de cada candidato

Breno Barcelos (Missão) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Breno Barcelos tem 41 anos e é candidato a um cargo eletivo pela primeira vez. Durante sua campanha, a Segurança Pública foi um tema em evidência: entre as propostas que mais tiveram destaque, estão a eliminação de facções criminosas e a reocupação de territórios dominados por essas organizações.

“A criminalidade tem crescido no Espírito Santo, diferente do que o atual governador falou [...] Nossa prioridade é o combate ao crime organizado, não só na atuação dentro das comunidades, mas também na asfixia financeira desse crime organizado”, disse o candidato em entrevista ao Gazeta Meio Dia , da TV Gazeta .

O candidato propôs, ainda, a construção de um presídio de segurança máxima para membros de facções — inspirado no modelo adotado no Centro de Confinamiento del Terrorismo (CECOT) de El Salvador.

Em seus discursos e publicações nas redes sociais, Breno Barcelos também destacou o plano de desfavelização do Espírito Santo e a realocação dessas famílias. O projeto, de acordo com o candidato, também engloba o desenvolvimento da infraestrutura desses locais, a implantação de escolas cívico-militares e melhorias relacionadas ao comércio e a cultura.

O candidato realizou eventos de campanha na Região Metropolitana e também no Norte, Noroeste e Sul do Espírito Santo.

Helder Salomão (PT), candidato ao governo do Espírito Santo — Foto: Carlos Alberto Silva/Rede Gazeta

Helder Salomão é professor e exerce atualmente o terceiro mandato consecutivo como deputado federal.

Em sua campanha, o ex-prefeito de Cariacica destacou que é o candidato apoiado por Lula no Espírito Santo e suas propostas para a Educação. Entre os projetos divulgados pelo candidato para a área estão a criação de uma política estadual de cuidado e saúde mental para professores, a ampliação do ensino integral e o cumprimento do piso salarial nacional para a classe.

"Eu coloquei no nosso programa de governo, depois de ouvir muitos professores, que a gente vai implantar no Espírito Santo, para todos os servidores, mas em especial para os professores, a política estadual de cuidado e de saúde mental", declarou Helder Salomão durante entrevista ao vivo no Gazeta Meio Dia , da TV Gazeta .

O candidato também abordou o enfrentamento a violência contra as mulheres e ao feminicídio, com destaque para a proposta de implantação de um Pacto Estadual pelo Enfrentamento às Violências contra a Mulher e Prevenção ao Feminicídio e de auxílio financeiro para mulheres vítimas de violência. Durante sua campanha, Helder Salomão cumpriu agendas de campanha na Grande Vitória e também no interior do estado.

Lorenzo Pazolini (Republicanos), candidato ao governo do Espírito Santo — Foto: Carlos Alberto Silva/Rede Gazeta

Ex-prefeito de Vitória, Lorenzo Pazolini já foi auditor do Tribunal de Contas do Espírito Santo (TC-ES) e teve carreira na Polícia Civil do estado antes de entrar para a vida política. Durante sua campanha, o candidato destacou os feitos de seu mandato na prefeitura da capital.

“Muito além de números, de índices, de qualificação, o mais importante é ter a sensibilidade, estar ao lado da população capixaba no momento em que ela mais precisa. Foi assim que nós transformamos Vitória em referência nacional em saúde, educação, qualificação e em qualidade de vida, mas, principalmente, em uma cidade humana, que valoriza a arte, cultura, entretenimento e lazer, que se tornou referência nacional em qualidade de vida”, disse o candidato no debate promovido pela TV Gazeta .

Em sua campanha, Pazolini também ressaltou suas propostas para a Educação e a Saúde. Entre os projetos estão o fim das filas de consultas e exames, a ampliação de leitos, a criação de Centros de Atenção Psicossocial (Caps) e o apoio financeiro para municípios na atenção básica.

O candidato prometeu, ainda, concluir a obra do Hospital Geral de Cariacica e o Complexo de Saúde Norte, em São Mateus, além de construir o novo Hospital Infantil Estadual.

Na área da Educação, o candidato propôs ampliar o ensino em tempo integral em todo o Espírito Santo. Pazolini abordou também o desenvolvimento regional e cumpriu agendas na Grande Vitória e no interior do estado.

Rafael Demuner (UP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Rafael Demuner é servidor público técnico-administrativo da Universidade Federal do Espírito Santo (Ufes) e coordenador estadual e nacional do Movimento Luta de Classes. Em sua campanha, o candidato destacou seu apoio ao fim da escala 6x1 e sua proposta de aumento de 100% do salário mínimo.

"Só que, com salário de R$ 1.621, a pessoa não consegue fazer isso porque não consegue fechar as contas no final do mês. Ela é empurrada para fazer renda complementar, fazer um 'bico'. Então, a UP defende um salário mínimo nacional duplicado, com aumento em 100%. No nosso Estado, a gente quer criar o salário mínimo capixaba no valor de R$ 3.242, que é exatamente a duplicação", disse Rafael Demuner em entrevista ao Gazeta Meio Dia , da TV Gazeta .

O candidato também defendeu a redução da jornada de trabalho para servidores estaduais e terceirizados para 36 horas semanais e a implantação da tarifa zero no transporte público. Destacou, também, a intenção de instituir um auxílio-aluguel estadual mínimo de R$ 1 mil e taxação de imóveis abandonados.

Durante sua campanha, o candidato cumpriu agendas em municípios da Grande Vitória e não realizou visitas ao interior do Espírito Santo.

Ricardo Ferraço (MDB), governador e candidato ao governo do Espírito Santo — Foto: Carlos Alberto Silva/Rede Gazeta

Ricardo Ferraço atuou como vice-governador do Espírito Santo a partir de 2023 e assumiu o cargo de governador do estado em abril deste ano após a saída de Renato Casagrande, que disputa uma vaga no Senado. Em sua campanha, o candidato destacou os feitos do mandato e o objetivo de dar continuidade ao trabalho realizado até então.

O candidato deu destaque a propostas nas áreas da Educação, Saúde e Segurança Pública e declarou que pretende fazer do Espírito Santo um dos estados mais seguros do país.

“Eu estou seguro e vou trabalhar todos os dias da minha vida até fazer do Espírito Santo um dos estados mais seguros do Brasil”, afirmou Ferraço em entrevista ao Gazeta Meio Dia, da TV Gazeta. Ele disse, ainda, que o estado terá 3.650 novos policiais militares até o fim do ano.

Em relação a área da Saúde, Ricardo Ferraço afirmou que o governo está construindo 108 unidades básicas de saúde e citou a construção de um hospital do câncer em parceria com o Hospital Evangélico em Cachoeiro de Itapemirim. Para a educação, destacou que pretende ampliar a educação integral e construir 144 novas creches, além de prometer aumento salarial para professores e um concurso público com 3 mil vagas para o cargo.

Ferraço cumpriu agendas de campanha em todas as regiões do estado.

articles.title: Viva + Via Costeira deste domingo é suspenso por causa das eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa que fecha trecho da Via Costeira para a prática de esporte e lazer aos domingos será retomada no dia 11.
articles.summary: Iniciativa que fecha trecho da Via Costeira para a prática de esporte e lazer aos domingos será retomada no dia 11.
articles.body:
O projeto Viva + Via Costeira não será realizado neste domingo (4), em Natal, por conta da realização das eleições. A medida foi anunciada pela Secretaria de Estado do Turismo (Setur).

Projeto Viva + Via Costeira fecha trecho da Via Costeira, em Natal, para a prática de atividades esportivas e de lazer — Foto: Divulgação/Assecom

A ação que transforma um trecho da Via Costeira em um espaço de convivência, lazer, esporte e bem-estar será retomada no dia 11 de outubro, das 16h às 19h.

De acordo com a Setur, o Viva + Via Costeira tem o objetivo de incentivar a ocupação dos espaços públicos, promovendo qualidade de vida, integração social e o contato da população com um dos principais cartões-postais de Natal.

articles.title: In 1952, John Steinbeck wrote a novel, putting in some of his own family’s history in California’s Salinas Valley; half a century later, Florence Pugh starred in the drama series that drew on the biblical story of dark impulses

articles.body: Imagine writing a story, drawing inspiration from your family drama, and over 50 years later, that same story shows up on our screens, winning the audience globally!Per History.com, back in 1952, John Steinbeck sat down to write a story that felt almost too close to home. East of Eden wasn't just a novel to him; it was his attempt to pin down what made his family, and maybe even himself, tick. He poured into its pages memories of California’s Salinas Valley, the home turf where his mother’s people, the Hamiltons, had built their lives. But Steinbeck wasn’t just interested in tracing his own roots. He wanted to dig deeper, to understand what drives families apart, or pulls them together, over generations.Steinbeck found a mirror in one of the oldest tales around: Cain and Abel, that biblical story of two brothers locked in an endless struggle of jealousy and yearning. Steinbeck wove his family history together with that ancient story. So, while ‘East of Eden’ has the rolling farmlands and wild edges of California, it’s also haunted by bigger questions: Why do we hurt the ones we love?Moreover, is our fate set by what’s come before, or do we ever get to make our own choices?Decades later, these questions haven’t faded. If anything, they're just as sharp in the world of streaming TV. Netflix’s new adaptation, with Florence Pugh stepping into the shoes of the enigmatic Cathy Ames, picks up where Steinbeck left off. This isn’t your typical period drama. The show asks, just as the book did: Are we stuck repeating our parents’ mistakes, or can we carve out a new path? That question, raw and uncomfortable, still hangs in the air.Why did Steinbeck write East of Eden in the first place?Honestly, he’d been living with the idea for years before he finally put pen to paper. He called it the “big one”: the book he had to write. But his reason was pretty simple: He wanted to tell his sons, Thom and John, where they came from. He wanted them to know their family’s story; not just the facts, but the tangled emotions and hidden battles that made their family what it was. The Hamiltons in the novel pretend to be fictional, but they wear the faces of Steinbeck’s real relatives. At the same time, he invented the Trask family and used their stormy relationships to ask deeper questions about love, betrayal, and forgiveness.Steinbeck didn’t hold back from putting himself in the story, either. He made himself a character in the book: interrupting, reflecting, and sometimes almost arguing with his own memories. It’s not just historical fiction; it’s almost part family album, part confession.But underneath all of this runs the original engine: the story of Cain and Abel. You know the basics: two brothers, one loved a little less, anger festering until tragedy strikes. Steinbeck believed this wasn’t just an old story, but a blueprint for human pain. He once called it “the basis of all human neurosis,” and in East of Eden, he repeats it: first with Adam and Charles Trask, then with Cal and Aron. The names make it obvious: if you’re looking for biblical parallels, you can’t miss them. One brother wants to be seen as good; the other is haunted by jealousy, desperate to be chosen.But Steinbeck wasn’t interested in copying the Bible. He wanted to ask: does it have to be this way? Are we doomed to act out old scripts, or can we change the ending? That’s where “timshel” comes in. This Hebrew word pops up in the middle of Cain’s story in the Bible, and in Steinbeck’s novel, the character Lee insists it means “thou mayest.” In other words, you have a choice. You aren’t stuck being the villain in your own family’s drama.And then there’s Cathy Ames, the character Florence Pugh plays in the new show. Cathy is not just a black-and-white antagonist. In the novel, she’s unsettling, complicated, and capable of incredible harm. But Zoe Kazan, who created the Netflix series, wanted to get closer to her. She didn’t just want to show Cathy as evil; she wanted to open her up, to ask what made her that way, and to show how society sometimes decides what “kind” of woman someone is and punishes her for it. In this version, Cathy isn’t just a force of chaos; she’s a person with motives, fears, and her own wounds.The Salinas Valley, though, is maybe the quietest character in the story. Steinbeck grew up among its ranches and farms, catching the rhythms of life and loss that echo throughout East of Eden. This isn’t just setting; it’s inheritance. The land holds stories: some passed down with pride, others handed off like burdens. Even though the Netflix series was filmed thousands of miles away in New Zealand, it worked hard to bring the Valley’s weird light and sense of possibility to life.East of Eden has lasted because these questions, about family, destiny, and the darkness we try to outrun, never really go away. Whether it’s Steinbeck worrying about his sons, or Florence Pugh’s Cathy testing the boundaries of who she can be, the heart of the story endures: How much of who we are is in our blood, and how much is up to us? That question still burns, stubborn as ever.Maybe that’s why, after all these years, East of Eden keeps coming back, asking new generations to look inward and ask: “Who am I, really, and can I choose a different way?”You use AI every day. articles.title: Newent baby bank 'open to everybody'
articles.summary: The facility offers essential items for free, including clothes for babies and small children.
articles.body:
The lead volunteer of a new baby bank, which gives away free children's products to those in need, says it is "open to everybody".

The Newent hub of Forest of Dean Baby Bank at The Ark Cafe in Newent, Gloucestershire, offers everything from baby wipes and breast pumps to hats and swimwear, and can also source larger items like cots from a warehouse in Cinderford.

Helen Carter, lead volunteer, says no one will be means tested, with parents often picking up new items while donating what no longer fits their child.

Kylie, a Newent mum visiting the baby bank, said: "It's always expensive to buy new baby things and food and nappies and wipes. So to have the support locally is wonderful."

Company fined after worker dies in first-floor fall

Why is Gloucester City Council still leaderless?

First Restore Britain councillor in the West

A lot of the items available at the faciltity are donated, which Carter said the team was "really, really grateful for".

Currently, autumn clothing bundles are in demand, but volunteers have already started putting together a Christmas box of festive clothing, blankets, and shoes.

"A lot of people say, 'I don't need it, I'm okay', but then a lot of people are just sort of managing their finances and are unable to have a nice day out with their children," Carter said.

"But if they [visit the baby bank], then they would be able to pay for that day out, so they might not think they're struggling, but it helps."

In its latest Parent Experience Report, The National Childbirth Trust said nearly half of parents said they were struggling more financially after having a baby, a figure which rose to about six in ten among self-employed, unemployed or part-time employed parents.

Kylie, who was on her first visit to the bank, said clothing and supplies for children were "always expensive".

"I'm quite lucky, I do have an older child as well, so I've got a lot of hand-me-downs," she said.

"But for everyone who hasn't got an older child and [do] formula feeding and things like that, it is very expensive to keep them clean and fed."

Volunteer Isabel said she wanted to give back to the centre after she was helped with food parcels and clothing.

"I know from having three small children that there is a massive need in the area, so I think this is a great thing that we're doing here," she said.

"I just wish more people knew about it."

The baby bank is open every Tuesday morning from 09.30 to 11.30.

articles.title: Ancient Wimbleball Lake bridge revealed by continued low levels
articles.summary: The Bessom Bridge on Exmoor was flooded nearly 50 years ago when Wimbleball Reservoir was created.
articles.body:
Months of dry weather and prolonged heat have revealed a bridge dating back to the Victorian times that had been submerged during the creation of a reservoir.

The ancient stone Bessom Bridge flooded nearly 50 years ago when Wimbleball Reservoir was created at Exmoor National Park in Somerset. It was later replaced by a new bridge.

In the summer, the Environment Agency declared that Wimbleball was one of the top three lowest reservoirs in the country after levels were recorded as "exceptionally low".

Dr Lucy Shipley, historic environment record officer for Exmoor, said: "We live in an ever-changing world and it's not a kind of fixed point where things stay the same."

Teenage boy, 16, killed in motorbike crash

Complaints about animal sales at Bridgwater Fair

Ted Lasso honours Anthony Head with fresh tribute

Shipley said there were other archaeological finds beneath the lake which were not demolished before the reservoir were created, including a barrow dating back to the Bronze Age.

It is not known why some structures were demolished and others were not.

The former Bessom Bridge used to cross a stream that fed into the River Haddeo, while the new one crosses the north side of the lake.

When water levels drop, the old bridge can be seen from the new one.

Shipley said the changing landscape on Exmoor was "extraordinary".

"The photographs are incredible, they're just so dramatic of the bridge poking out from the silt and sediment that's covered it.

"We live in an ever-changing world and it's not a kind of fixed point where things stay the same, but then by contrast… there's been a consistency of settlement and people living in farming and working in similar ways, so it's that balance of understanding how the world around us is always changing and responding, but also recognising that some things are really consistent over time."

She added that the historic bridge could be enjoyed from afar and asked visitors to refrain from walking on the dried-up section of the reservoir.

Elsewhere around the county, traces of centuries-old gardens were found in Bishop's Palace in Wells , while relics of old structures were uncovered at Glastonbury Abbey due to the record-breaking summer temperatures .

Wimbeball Reservoir, which supplies water to hundreds of thousands of homes across the South West, has a capacity of 21,320 megalitres - one megalitre is a million litres.

The reservoir remains low following record-breaking temperatures over the summer, with a current capacity of only 21.1% as of 27 September, according to South West Water.

Hundreds of thousands of people remain under hosepipe bans across the country while water sources recover from the prolonged dry weather.

The National Drought Group said the recent rain has not been enough to replenish supplies, with drought only being over when rivers, groundwater and reservoirs return to normal levels.

Research from the Environment Agency showed the country will need 120% of typical rainfall over the next seven months for all areas to be considered out of drought.

articles.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with crash axe in ‘terrorist act’: UAE
articles.summary: Probe ⁠under way to determine ‘all the ⁠circumstances’, including motive, UAE’s prosecutor general says.
articles.body:
The prosecutor general of the United Arab Emirates has said a Flydubai co-pilot “attempted to carry out a terrorist act” during a flight earlier this week, using a crash axe against the pilot inside the cockpit.

State news agency WAM quoted Hamad Saif al-Shamsi as saying on Saturday that the attacker of Wednesday’s flight FZ1073 tried to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls.

He said the investigation is under way “to uncover all the circumstances of the incident, its motives, and related connections, in addition to completing technical examinations and examining physical and digital evidence”.

The final results will be announced as soon as the necessary procedures are completed, al-Shamsi said.

A crash axe is a tool kept in a cockpit to help pilots cut through the plane in emergencies.

The plane carrying 174 passengers was on its way from the UAE’s Dubai to Israel’s Tel Aviv on Wednesday when a co-pilot wounded Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who opened the cockpit to seek help.

The attacker was not officially identified, but media reports quoting unnamed sources claimed he was Omani national Hamam al-Hammami .

The aircraft briefly plunged about 17,000 feet (5,180 metres) before it was brought back under control by a second paid of new pilots after passengers and crew subdued the attacker.

The flight was diverted and forced to make an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia.

The co-pilot was arrested by Saudi authorities and handed over to the UAE as it leads the probe.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that ⁠Israel was looking into whether the co-pilot had acted under anyone’s direction, warning that anyone involved would pay a “heavy price”.

Flydubai halted all flights its Israel route after the incident and Israel’s El Al cancelled its scheduled flights, stranding some Israelis in the UAE.

At 22:00 GMT on Friday, the first repatriation flight, operated by Israeli carrier Arkia, arrived at Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport from Dubai.

articles.title: Guernsey hosts inter-island environment meeting
articles.summary: The annual event brings together delegates to share ideas and develop joint projects.
articles.body:
Environmental experts, conservation groups and businesses from across the British Isles and France have gathered in Guernsey for the 26th Inter-Island Environment Meeting.

The annual event, co-ordinated by the Guernsey Nature Commission, brings together delegates to share ideas and develop joint projects aimed at protecting the natural environment.

This year's theme, Nature for the Next Generation, includes talks on subjects ranging from seabird restoration and woodland resilience to butterfly monitoring in Sark and citizen science projects.

A Sixth Form Environment Meeting gave young people the chance to present environmental issues that matter to them and contribute ideas for the future.

Students will take part in workshops linked to Guernsey's upcoming Marine Spatial Plan, helping shape discussions about the future protection and management of the island's seas.

Angela Salmon, head of education at the Nature Commission and a member of the meeting group said inviting sixth formers to share the environmental issues that mattered to them "makes perfect sense".

Among those attending was Sebastian Dufour, an independent consultant for the Alderney Wildlife Trust, who joined a field trip to Lihou Island exploring its ecology and archaeology.

He said he had learned about a Benedictine Priory site "which is very interesting" and discovered there had been "a really remarkably large industry in harvesting seaweed".

Dufour said he particularly valued the collaborative nature of the event, adding: "We're all coming from different islands and we're all facing similar challenges."

He said the annual meeting provided an opportunity to "learn from each other" and "share our successes and failures and everything".

articles.title: I wish we'd pushed sooner, says wife of cancer patient
articles.summary: Natalie's husband Craig Sullivan, from Nottinghamshire, has stage four pancreatic cancer.
articles.body:
When Craig Sullivan started getting stomach pain, he put it down to a stressful house move and having a lot on at work.

At 44, Craig's stomach issues were initially put down to irritable bowel syndrome.

However, his condition worsened and, after tests and scans, the father of two was diagnosed with stage four pancreatic cancer a year later.

His wife Natalie, from Ruddington in Nottinghamshire, says: "I wish we'd pushed for more help sooner."

Craig's friends and family have now come together to raise money for private treatment, which they hope will prolong his life.

Under current guidelines, he cannot have those treatments on the NHS because of the type of cancer he has.

"I don't even think I could put into words how devastating it's been," Natalie adds.

"You have that thing when you wake up in the morning and for a second you don't think about it. And then you do.

"People don't realise it's not just about potentially losing someone you love, it's that your whole life changes in a second."

Natalie took Craig to A&E at Queen's Medical Centre (QMC) in Nottingham after he woke up with yellow eyes and skin.

Initially, he was told the yellowing could have been caused by blockages or gallstones, but a later scan showed he had a mass on his pancreas.

Craig, now 45, was given six rounds of chemotherapy to try to shrink the tumour in his pancreas so it could be removed.

"The tumour had shrunk by half by April, but [the doctors] still weren't comfortable operating," Natalie recalls. "So they wanted to do more chemo."

However, Craig became unwell due to an infection, and his chemotherapy was cancelled.

A subsequent scan showed the cancer had spread and further tumours had been found in his liver.

Pancreatic cancer can be found anywhere in the pancreas, and may not have any symptoms, according to the NHS .

It most commonly affects people who are over the age of 65, those who have medical conditions like chronic pancreatitis and those with a family history of pancreatic cancer.

the whites of your eyes or your skin turn yellow

itchy skin, darker pee and paler poo than usual

a high temperature, or feeling hot, cold or shivery

On average, 136 people aged under 45 are diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in the UK annually, according to figures by Pancreatic Cancer UK. This age group make up 1.1% of cases.

Something that has frustrated Craig and Natalie is the lack of options for treatment.

They said they were determined to find an alternative treatment using the money raised by their friends and family.

Natalie said she would also like to see more research into the disease.

According to Pancreatic Cancer UK , about 3% of all money invested into cancer research in the UK goes towards looking at pancreatic cancer.

Senior policy advisor for the charity, Charlotte Lynch, added: "Pancreatic cancer is really hard to diagnose, which is why people get diagnosed quite late because symptoms are often vague.

"The treatments for the disease are also really harsh and have severe side effects so sometimes people are just too unwell to have them."

She said they were regularly lobbying the government for more funding to go into research.

A Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) spokesperson said: "We know there is more to do to ensure that people are getting the care they deserve.

"That's why we are piloting a targeted approach that searches patient records to find people most at risk of pancreatic cancer, which could give more people a fighting chance and spare the heartbreak of countless families."

NHS England said decisions on which treatments were available on the NHS were made by the National Institute of Clinical Excellence (NICE).

In a statement, a spokesman said decisions on which treatments to offer patients were made based on "the benefits and risks" of using them in individual cases.

Friends and family of Craig and Natalie are hoping to raise £50,000 to pay for further private treatment in either Oxford or Germany.

It would not cure him, but could give him extra time with his sons, 14-year-old Alfie and 10-year-old Quinn.

Natalie said they had been "overwhelmed by the support" ahead of a charity football event on Saturday at the Pelican Colts football club, in Lenton Lane, where Craig used to be a coach.

One of the organisers, Laura Burton, said: "We're hoping it will be a great family day out, and it will raise vital funds for Craig.

"The community has really come together to support Craig and Natalie and their boys.

"Ruddington is not a big place but there's a huge community gathering for them, and it's heartwarming to see the efforts people have gone to."

articles.title: ‘Trauma still there’: A decades-old standoff returns to Northern Ireland
articles.summary: Families who lived through one of the Troubles’ worst flashpoints fear its legacy is reaching another generation.
articles.body:
Portadown, Northern Ireland – When the summer holidays arrived, Chris Nelson worried about his mother.

At night, he lay awake waiting for her to return. During the day, he rang family members to ask if she was safe. There were threats and letters through the door.

“I was afraid to leave the house,” he told Al Jazeera.

His mother, Rosemary Nelson, was a lawyer representing the Catholic residents opposing the Protestant Orange Order parade along Portadown’s Garvaghy Road in Northern Ireland in the late 1990s.

Every July, as marching season approached, there was a standoff.

Orangemen sought to return from Drumcree church along what they regarded as their traditional route. Residents opposed the passage of the anti-Catholic organisation through a majority Catholic street. In some years, police forced the parade through. In later years, it was blocked.

Rosemary would spend summer evenings alongside the residents on Garvaghy Road. Before leaving home each evening, she told her son that she was going to look after families and make sure their children were okay. She compared them to his friends at primary school.

“She was a big believer in helping the underdog,” said Chris, now 39. “She did a lot of work for free.”

His mother helped people from both sides of the community. When work allowed, the family went to Bundoran, across the border, and for a day the fear would pass.

But one night, during a standoff in 1997 when the state police force, the Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC), used batons to clear Catholic locals from the road, “she was beaten by the police”, said Chris. “She was spat on”, bruised and bloodied.

“That was very traumatic. I was always thinking something was going to happen to my mum.”

On a Monday in March 1999, nearly a year after the Good Friday Agreement brought an end to the conflict, Rosemary drove away from her home in Lurgan.

As she braked at a nearby junction, a bomb beneath her car exploded. Her eight-year-old daughter, Sarah, was at primary school nearby and heard the blast. The family had spent the previous weekend in Bundoran together.

Chris, 11 at the time, and his older brother were away on a school ski trip when they received a phone call with the news of her death.

“That was hard”, he said, his voice tailing off.

Nearly three decades later, another standoff has recast these childhood memories into fears for the next generation, with a renewed attempt by the Protestant Orange Order to march through the Catholic neighbourhood, threatening to unravel a fragile peace.

The Troubles began in the late 1960s as protests by Catholics against discrimination were met by repression and violence. Republican paramilitaries fought for a united Ireland as loyalists and the army battled to preserve British rule, in a conflict that killed more than 3,500 people.

The 1998 Good Friday Agreement established a framework for peace and power-sharing.

Under the agreement, the people of Portadown have lived in relative peace for the past 28 years.

But this was suddenly unsettled by a last-minute decision by the High Court to allow the march. In response, Catholic residents blocked the road. Many camped out as Orange men gathered at the top of the road, awaiting police permission to pass – an image of division that never truly left.

Many of the Garvaghy Road residents are now parents, and fear what their children might inherit from a dispute they hoped had been left behind.

Paul O’Connor, of the Pat Finucane Centre human rights group in Northern Ireland, said Rosemary Nelson is among 21 people whose deaths were linked to the Drumcree dispute.

Many are still being investigated, with families continuing to seek justice and pressing for public inquiries amid concerns about collusion between the British state and loyalist paramilitaries, many of which were members of the Orange Order.

“These murders encompass LVF (Loyal Volunteer Force) killings at that time, and are all linked to the Drumcree disputes. They were responsible for many of the killings around the Mid Ulster area at that time. They were trying to destabilise the peace process, with many riots spreading around, including into Derry,” O’Connor told Al Jazeera.

He worked with Rosemary Nelson and is now seeking a public inquiry into the murder of Sean Brown, another Drumcree-linked case, he believes. The 61-year-old father of six from Bellaghy, County Derry, was abducted and murdered in May 1997.

The following year, the three Quinn brothers – Richard, 10, Mark, nine, and Jason, eight – died after loyalists petrol-bombed their home in Ballymoney, County Antrim, as they slept. Their deaths, during the unrest surrounding Drumcree, brought widespread calls for the Orange Order to end its standoff.

In Portadown town centre, a Union flag flies among plinths dedicated to the Ulster Defence Regiment, a locally recruited unit of the British army and the Ulster Covenant – a document signed when nearly 500,000 people opposed a form of self-government for Ireland in 1912.

Around the corner, in the Edgarstown housing estate, Ulster Volunteer Force (UVF) flags hang from lampposts, and the kerbs are painted red, white and blue, alongside a mural of a Rangers FC badge.

The area is one of the heartlands of unionism. The Orange Order was founded in 1795 in the village of Loughgall, a few miles from Drumcree.

The Orangemen say they have marched the route through Garvaghy Road since 1807. The parade has been blocked from Garvaghy Road since 1998, but the Orangemen have continued submitting requests to march.

The latest Parades Commission decision permitted 35 men to walk without music. Since then, Orangemen have repeatedly approached the police line before returning to the church.

Irish nationalists have criticised the police assessment underpinning the decision to allow the march, while unionists have denounced police for failing to forcibly remove protesters blocking the route.

Al Jazeera contacted the three main unionist parties – the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP), the Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV) and the Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) – for comment but received no response.

Addressing around 200 supporters in Portadown, loyalist activist Jamie Bryson described protesters as “an unlawful snarling mob”.

He has called for the First Minister, Sinn Fein’s Michelle O’Neill, and police Chief Constable Jon Boutcher to resign, and demands that the Orange men must be allowed to walk the Garvaghy Road.

O’Neill has faced criticism for standing beside the protesters.

At Drumcree Church, the Orangemen were not marching, but sitting down drinking tea and eating crisps. Around six men, one wearing his sash, huddled under a gazebo in the cold.

“We are waiting patiently for the chief constable to apply the law of the land,” Nigel Dawson, the Portadown Orange Order district master, told Al Jazeera.

“Portadown District has never in its history stopped a parade down the road to have a confrontation with its neighbours, ever. So I don’t know where the fear and trepidation comes from.”

Another Orangeman, who requested anonymity, added: “We are determined to get home after Sunday service … We just want to go home.”

Around a mile further down the Garvaghy Road, Irish folk band the Mary Wallopers performed to hundreds of residents and supporters.

Children danced and slid down the embankment, as parents watched from above. Palestine and Ireland flags flew in the wind.

Linda O’Neill, 51, a Garvaghy Road resident, told Al Jazeera the scene would have been unimaginable 30 years ago.

“It was horrendous growing up as a teenager. We stayed in our own community. We didn’t access the town centre … This community was a ghetto. And that was deliberate.”

Another resident, Ciaran O Ferghail, remembered summers spent surrounded by British forces.

“This community was turned into a war zone. There were tanks and British Army everywhere, thousands of RUC. This community was completely under siege every summer, by the Orange Order, the British military, the RUC and loyalist paramilitaries. We were surrounded on every road and in every direction.”

O’Neill said the confrontation changed as residents began asserting their rights.

In 1995, hundreds sat down on Garvaghy Road to block the parade. The ensuing violent standoff between security forces and Orangemen and their loyalist supporters ended in a compromise allowing the march through. Residents say they understood it would be the last.

But the following summer, the parade returned. Police initially blocked it, then reversed course after five days of widespread loyalist attacks. Officers forced residents off the road and beat them, sparking riots in Catholic communities.

In 1997, security forces sealed off the Catholic neighbourhood before dawn and allowed the parade through at midday amid loyalist threats to kill Catholics if it was stopped. Nationalist protests and violence followed. From 1998, the march was banned from Garvaghy Road. But for residents, summers remained marked by the army’s steel barricades until 2000.

Chris Nelson, almost 40, is around the same age his mother was when she was killed.

The Garvaghy Road protests mark the first time he has chosen to speak publicly about his mother.

He went on to study law at university, but says his life would have followed a different trajectory if she were still here.

The public inquiry into his mother’s death found no evidence that state security agencies had “directly facilitated” her murder, but it “could not exclude the possibility” that individual members of those agencies had helped the perpetrators.

The inquiry brought the past back repeatedly as he tried to get on with his life. But seeing photographs of families linking arms on Garvaghy Road brought back unavoidable memories of his mother.

“If she were here, that’s where she would be,” he said, “standing with the people of the Garvaghy Road”.

While there has been no violence in Portadown, in Derry’s Waterside, two recent nights of disorder saw petrol bombs and masonry thrown at police. Officers described the crowd on the second night as mostly young people.

The renewed attempt to bring the Orange Order parade through Garvaghy Road risks leaving its mark on children on both sides. With some schools closed, Chris Nelson worries about parents having to explain to their kids what is happening.

“Children don’t forget things“, he said. “They absorb everything.”

He remembers how it felt waiting for his mother each night, and how that worry followed him through the summer holidays. He wants something different for the children growing up now.

“Children shouldn’t grow up knowing the difference between Catholic and Protestant.

“It isn’t something that should be brought into the mind of a child.”
