articles.summary: What started with one little lemonade stand in Ohio has become a powerful source of comfort for children facing illness, homelessness, foster care and
articles.body: What started with one little lemonade stand in Ohio has become a powerful source of comfort for children facing illness, homelessness, foster care and other hardships. In the summer of 2018, six-year-old Payton Obert raised $768 by selling lemonade and used every dollar to buy new toys for patients at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center. Eight years later, her idea has grown into Payton’s Lemonade Stand, a registered nonprofit that has generated more than $5 million in cash and donated goods for over 40 local organisations, according to Payton’s Lemonade Stand's website and the Cincinnati Open.A teddy bear that inspired a missionPayton’s wish to help children at the hospital came from personal experience. Years earlier, she had been a patient at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center and received a teddy bear during her stay. The toy offered comfort at a difficult time, and she continued to keep it beside her even after returning home. That small act of kindness stayed with her. When Payton set up her first lemonade stand in 2018, she was not hoping to earn money for herself. She wanted other children in hospital rooms to receive new toys that could bring reassurance, distraction and a reason to smile during frightening or unfamiliar days.The response was far bigger than anyone expected. Her first stand brought in $768, all of which went towards purchasing toys for young patients. It was a modest sum in the world of philanthropy, but its impact was immediate and deeply personal, laying the groundwork for a campaign that would eventually mobilise thousands of people, as per Payton’s Lemonade Stand's website.From one stand to a neighbourhood movementThe site further shared that Payton returned to the lemonade stand in 2019, but this time the idea had caught the attention of friends, neighbours and local supporters. The second annual event raised nearly $7,000, showing that the community was ready to rally around a child-led effort with a clear and heartfelt purpose. In 2020, the project expanded through the launch of Payton’s Pals, with eight additional lemonade stands opening across Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. Despite the disruption and uncertainty of the Covid-19 pandemic, the third annual campaign raised more than $35,000. The results showed that even in difficult circumstances, people were willing to support a simple act of kindness rooted in a child’s desire to help others.The annual event soon became more than a family fundraiser. It turned into a day when children, parents, neighbourhood groups, schools and businesses could all play a role in giving back. A glass of lemonade became the starting point for conversations about empathy, community responsibility and the difference small actions can make.Becoming an official nonprofitAs donations grew, Payton’s mission widened beyond hospital toy drives. In 2021, Payton’s Lemonade Stand officially became a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organisation, enabling it to work with hospitals, shelters, schools and child-focused community groups. The central goal remained the same: provide practical support and moments of joy to children experiencing hardship. That year, more than 100 young hosts organised 30 lemonade stands and raised $60,000 in a single day. The movement continued to build momentum in 2022, when more than 200 children took part in 50 stands supported by fire departments, soccer teams, Girl Scout troops, local businesses and families. Together, they raised $85,000.The growth reflected the appeal of Payton’s original idea. It did not require participants to have large budgets, professional fundraising experience or access to major donor networks. It asked people to set up a simple stand, invite their neighbours and direct the proceeds toward children who needed support.Reaching thousands of childrenPayton’s Lemonade Stand now supports more than 40 local organisations that distribute assistance to children and families, as per Cincinnati Open. The nonprofit’s help comes in many forms, including funds, toys, clothing, coats, food and other essentials. Its partners include organisations working with children in hospitals, shelters, schools, foster care and low-income households.This broader focus recognises that hardship does not look the same for every child. Some may be undergoing medical treatment, while others may lack warm clothing, stable housing or basic school supplies. By collaborating with trusted local groups, the nonprofit can respond to needs identified by people already working closely with vulnerable families. The approach also keeps the impact rooted in the Greater Cincinnati community. Donations are directed to organisations that understand local challenges and can distribute aid quickly. That local focus helps turn each lemonade stand into practical help for children who may be facing difficult circumstances close to home.The biggest year yetThe campaign crossed the $100,000 mark in one day in 2023 and went further in 2024, raising more than $125,000. In 2025, the eighth annual Payton’s Lemonade Stand featured more than 100 stands across Ohio, Kentucky and Indiana. In just three hours, the community raised more than $150,000, according to Payton’s Lemonade Stand's website.The locations reflected how widely the idea had travelled. Stands were hosted not only in front yards but also at Kings Island, senior living communities and local businesses. The expansion demonstrated that a project started by a six-year-old could create opportunities for people of different ages and backgrounds to contribute to the same cause.By 2026, the overall effort had raised more than $5 million in monetary and in-kind donations. That total represents a remarkable leap from the original $768 stand, but the organisation still centres its work on the simple belief that every child deserves to feel seen, supported and cared for.Recognition for a young changemakerPayton Obert was named among the Cincinnati Open and Fifth Third Bank’s 2026 Cincy Serves honourees, a group of 11 local residents recognised for making a positive difference in Greater Cincinnati. Each honouree received a $5,300 donation for the charity of their choice as well as a VIP experience at the 2026 Cincinnati Open.The recognition placed Payton alongside volunteers, advocates and nonprofit leaders working across education, disability inclusion, financial support, health and community safety. Her place on the list was a reminder that meaningful civic leadership does not depend on age. It can begin with a child who remembers the comfort of a teddy bear and decides to pass that feeling on.Payton’s story continues to resonate and inspire people because it is both extraordinary and accessible. Few six-year-olds launch a nonprofit that reaches millions of dollars in support, yet the first step was something almost anyone can understand: sharing lemonade with neighbours and using the proceeds to brighten another child’s day.You use AI every day. This week I’m hoping to be right about this matchup between Florida and Missouri. The Florida Gators come into this game with a 4-0 record and are coming off of arguably the most impressive victory in College Football this season. The Gators hosted Ole Miss last week, and they rocked the Rebels. In fairness, this was a trap, and I did mention it in a preview I provided in a different article. They were able to win 44-39 in that game, and they were up big for most of the game. However, late in the game, they gave up two touchdowns in the final eight minutes to make the game closer than it needed to be. Missouri is the 25th-ranked team in the country, and they currently sit at 3-1 for the year. They opened the season with a win over Arkansas Pine Bluff. It wasn’t much of a contest, with a 40-point win over the Golden Lions. The following week, they did have a bit of a challenge as they faced Kansas and won on the road with a 17-point victory over the Jayhawks. Week 3 saw them take on Troy and win by 10. He has been really strong in almost every game. Last week he threw for 295 yards and three touchdowns. He won’t really run the ball, rushing 10 times for 1 yard this season, so he will look to attack the Gators through the air. It is hard to believe that the Gators are going to lose this game, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this is a tougher match than their game last week. articles.title: Why Alabama should cover against Mississippi State in a college football Week 5 prediction
articles.summary: Alabama football faces Mississippi State in a Week 5 clash, but the Crimson Tide's looming Georgia matchup could make this a dangerous trap game.
articles.body: Week 5 is here for college football, and Week 4 finally brought me a winning week in the sport. I’m hoping to build off that momentum and keep rolling. We’ve got some great games ahead of us this week, and the schedule is built for a full day of football watching. My first game starts early in the day as Alabama takes on Mississippi State. The Alabama Crimson Tide are 4-0, but something feels like this team isn’t quite as impressive as past years. They haven’t won a National Championship since the 2020 season. Since Nick Saban has left, they are 24-8, including this year’s 4-0 start. Certainly things have gotten more difficult for all teams, but Alabama’s success is slipping away as they continue to search for a new identity under Ken DeBoer. PAUL FINEBAUM’S PROCLAMATION ABOUT ALABAMA COACH KALEN DEBOER REIGNITES COLLEGE FOOTBALL ‘CULTURE FIT’ DEBATE So far, the team is ranked 7th in the nation, but they face a tough schedule ahead. This is the first of four games against ranked opponents in five weeks. This could be a trap week as well because they have Georgia at home next week, always one of the toughest teams in the country, and one of the toughest games on their schedule each season. Keelon Russell, the team’s quarterback, has looked solid in the past two games, throwing for seven touchdown passes and 685 yards. If he can be a difference-maker at the position, I expect Alabama to make a real run at the National Championship. The Mississippi State Bulldogs are 4-0 and currently the 16th ranked team in the country. They haven’t had an especially difficult schedule to start the season, but they did have a challenge last week as they beat Missouri. It was probably best for them that they were hosting the game, but even as the home team, it feels like Mississippi State is a tier below the top College Football Playoff teams. A win here would be big for his Heisman resume, and for Mississippi State pushing for a chance to get into the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately for the Bulldogs, I don’t feel like they are ready to get there, and I don’t think they’ll win this game. Alabama should win this one without much of an issue.
